items.title: Pre-COP Leaders’ Event in Fiji and Tuvalu
items.content_text: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Fiji and Tuvalu from 5 to 7 October 2026 for the Pre-COP Leaders’ event. At COP30, Australia secured the role of COP31 President of Negotiations and agreement to deliver a Pacific-hosted Pre-COP, including a special Leaders’ event. Australia will co-host the event with Fiji and Tuvalu.

items.title: Melbourne Airport Rail Stage 2 set for take-off
items.content_text: The Albanese and Carroll Labor Governments are getting on with building Melbourne Airport Rail Stage 2, with work set to begin in the coming weeks.It will include a new 7.4-kilometre rail line from Albion toward the Airport precinct via a brand-new Keilor East station, as part of the $12 billion joint commitment from the Albanese and Carroll Labor Governments.The line will connect directly to the Metro Tunnel and feature the same high-capacity signalling to enable frequent services.

items.title: Accelerating the delivery of more homes for South Australians
items.content_text: The Albanese and Malinauskas Governments are working together to fast-track more housing for South Australians, through the redevelopment of two key Defence sites near the Adelaide CBD.Hampstead Barracks was recently identified as a property for divestment, as part of the Australian Government’s response to the independent Defence Estate Audit. The Audit identified sites surplus to Defence’s need, with no clear or ongoing link to capabilities or keeping Australians safe.

We now know that it wasn't just the issue of the Australian sites that have been subject to AI agents accessing information without authorisation. There are dozens of cases, including US government sites.

items.content_text: My dear colleagues.This evening I want to talk about the need for nations to work together on the new challenges we face – climate change, emerging technology and the breakdown of international rules.Eight decades ago, the citizens and leaders of our nations made a solemn promise to future generations.Having known the ‘untold sorrow’ of two devastating global conflicts in their lifetimes, they vowed to work together to prevent another.

items.title: Press conference - New York
items.content_text: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Thanks for joining me. I want to update Australians on an incident in which an artificial intelligence agent has infiltrated an Australian Government website. This incident occurred in June of this year and involved an OpenAI agent gaining unauthorised access into the public-facing Medicare statistics reporting service portal, which is administered by Services Australia. The AI agent accessed both public and non-public files.

items.title: Agreement on long-term support and cooperation between Australia and Ukraine
items.content_text: Today Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed the Australia–Ukraine Bilateral Security Agreement. The Agreement provides a framework for defence and security cooperation and affirms Australia’s enduring commitment to Ukraine.After more than four years of defending itself against Russia’s unprovoked and unjustified invasion, Ukraine has developed one of the world’s most innovative and agile fighting forces.

items.title: P4M Summit: Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity
items.content_text: Colleagues, Australia has always been one of the world’s strongest supporters of the United Nations. Our position on its future and the future of global relations is clear – global challenges cannot be solved by countries acting alone. Especially right now, when we are facing one of the toughest periods in modern history. The war in the Middle East, an ongoing land war in Europe, the global inflation crisis, the fuel crisis and the rise of AI are incredibly serious challenges.

items.title: Australia launches bid for United Nations Security Council seat
items.content_text: At a time of global uncertainty and major challenges, Australia is an untiring advocate for peace and security. We understand that this is best achieved through international cooperation, which is why we are launching our campaign for a seat on the United Nations Security Council, to serve a two-year term from 2029 to 2030.

items.title: Australia ranked 8th in global gender equality rankings
items.content_text: Australia has ranked 8th in the World Economic Forum’s 2026 Global Gender Gap Report, breaking into to the top ten and achieving its highest ever ranking for gender equality, out of 148 countries.This result reflects the Albanese Government’s sustained action to improve the lives of women and girls, including lifting wages in female-dominated industries, expanding Paid Parental Leave to six months with superannuation, and making significant investments in women’s health.

items.title: Lasting Legacy: A new era for the Hunter as M1 extension opens
items.content_text: After more than four million hours of construction, the Hunter’s largest road infrastructure project will open to traffic in the early hours of 11 September, delivering a new 15-kilometre motorway connection between Black Hill and Raymond Terrace.The opening of the M1 Pacific Motorway extension marks a major milestone for the Hunter, closing a missing link in the Sydney to Brisbane economic corridor and strengthening one of Australia’s most important freight routes.
